# OpenApiFeatureFlags

> Feature flags for Swagger and OpenAPI documents on .NET. Mark an endpoint, action, parameter or
> schema property with [OpenApiFeatureFlag] and it only appears in the generated document while the
> flag is enabled. Gating is documentation-only: it never changes runtime behaviour.

## Packages

Eight packages, shipped in lockstep at one version:

- [OpenApiFeatureFlags](https://www.nuget.org/packages/OpenApiFeatureFlags): core planner and service registration.
- [OpenApiFeatureFlags.Abstractions](https://www.nuget.org/packages/OpenApiFeatureFlags.Abstractions): the attribute and contracts, dependency-free.
- [OpenApiFeatureFlags.Swashbuckle](https://www.nuget.org/packages/OpenApiFeatureFlags.Swashbuckle): adapter for Swashbuckle (AddSwaggerGen).
- [OpenApiFeatureFlags.AspNetCore](https://www.nuget.org/packages/OpenApiFeatureFlags.AspNetCore): adapter for the built-in Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi (net10.0 only).
- [OpenApiFeatureFlags.NSwag](https://www.nuget.org/packages/OpenApiFeatureFlags.NSwag): adapter for NSwag (AddOpenApiDocument).
- [OpenApiFeatureFlags.Analyzers](https://www.nuget.org/packages/OpenApiFeatureFlags.Analyzers): four Roslyn rules (OAFF1001, OAFF2001, OAFF3001, OAFF5001) that catch the silent authoring traps at build time.
- [OpenApiFeatureFlags.FeatureManagement](https://www.nuget.org/packages/OpenApiFeatureFlags.FeatureManagement): flag source for Microsoft.FeatureManagement.
- [OpenApiFeatureFlags.OpenFeature](https://www.nuget.org/packages/OpenApiFeatureFlags.OpenFeature): flag source for the CNCF OpenFeature standard.

## Quickstart

```csharp
builder.Services.AddOpenApiFeatureFlagsWithFeatureManagement();

builder.Services.AddSwaggerGen(options =>
{
    options.SwaggerDoc("v1", new OpenApiInfo { Title = "My API", Version = "1.0" });
    options.AddOpenApiFeatureFlagFilters();   // the Swashbuckle engine line
});
```

The engine line differs per engine: `options.AddOpenApiFeatureFlagFilters()` (Swashbuckle),
`options.AddOpenApiFeatureFlagTransformers()` (built-in), or
`settings.AddOpenApiFeatureFlagProcessors(services)` (NSwag). Mark gated elements with
`[OpenApiFeatureFlag("FlagName")]`; gate part of a description with `<gate flag="FlagName">...</gate>`
(escaped under NSwag: `&lt;gate flag="FlagName"&gt;...&lt;/gate&gt;`).

## Facts

- Engines: Swashbuckle; the built-in Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi (net10.0 only); NSwag. FastEndpoints v8.2 or later runs through the built-in engine.
- Flag providers: Microsoft.FeatureManagement, OpenFeature, or a custom IFeatureFlagSource. Azure App Configuration works through FeatureManagement.
- Modes: Remove (default), Annotate (adds x-feature-flag), Include.
- Guarantees: fail closed; throws FeatureFlagSourceUnavailableException rather than publish a document that silently lost gated endpoints (CanaryEnabled = false turns that off); byte-identical document when no attribute is used.
- Targets: net8.0, net9.0, net10.0. License: MIT. Tests: 647 runs across eight test projects.
- Not a security control: hiding an operation from the document leaves the endpoint routeable.

- [docs/aspnetcore.md](https://github.com/dogukandemir/OpenApiFeatureFlags/blob/main/docs/aspnetcore.md): the built-in-engine adapter, its net10.0 restriction, and the minimal-API parameter boundary.

- [docs/security.md](https://github.com/dogukandemir/OpenApiFeatureFlags/blob/main/docs/security.md): security posture and availability trade-offs.
